title: Power Problems
about: Make a battery last longer, and fix charging problems safely.

cards.prompt: No charger on a long trip: last **at least 8 hours** with **music** on. (**Low power mode** saves energy.)
cards.explanation: **Brightness**, **location** and **background apps** drain most; turn them down or use **low power mode**. Music uses very little.
cards.hint: Change one setting at a time and watch the power meter.
cards.nudge: Music uses very little; find what makes the power meter drop most.

cards.prompt: **Heat** wears batteries out. Does each habit **help** the battery, or **drain or damage** it?

items.label: Low power mode on a long day
Keeping it out of the hot sun
Leaving it in a hot car
Location on for every app, all day

cards.explanation: Dimming and low power mode save charge. **Heat** (hot cars, charging under a pillow) wears it out, and location all day drains it.
cards.hint: Heavy use and **heat** both hurt: which habits save energy or keep it cool?
cards.nudge: Trapped heat while charging counts too; anything running all day drains it.

cards.prompt: Your phone won't charge. Tip: cables wear out more often than phones, and **metal or water** can damage a [[port]].

steps.text: What's the simplest thing to try first?

choices.text: Try a different cable and a different plug socket
choices.consequence: Good: cables and chargers wear out far more often than phones.

choices.text: Poke a pin into the charging port to clean it
choices.consequence: Never put metal in the port. It can scratch the contacts or cause a [[short circuit]].

steps.text: That cable charges a friend's phone, but not yours. A torch shows the port is **packed with pocket fluff**.

choices.text: Phone off, an adult brushes it with a soft, dry brush
choices.consequence: Out comes the fluff, and it's charging! If not, a repair shop could clean it safely.

choices.text: Dig the fluff out carefully with a paper clip
choices.consequence: Metal can damage the port or short it out. Use something soft, or let a repair shop do it.

choices.text: Rinse the fluff out of the port with water
choices.consequence: Water and electronics don't mix. It could damage the phone for good.

cards.explanation: Try **another cable and socket** first. For fluff, with the phone off, an adult brushes it out with something soft and dry: **never metal, never water**, or ask a repair shop.
cards.hint: Simplest, safest fix first. For fluff: soft, dry, and an adult's help.

cards.prompt: Tap the **charging port**, where the fluff was hiding.
cards.explanation: The **charging port** is on the bottom edge, open to the outside, so fluff collects there.
cards.hint: It's where the charger plugs in, on one of the phone's edges.
cards.nudge: Where do you plug in a charger? That opening is on an outside edge.

cards.prompt: This tablet's port looks fluffy. Is each idea **safe to try**, or could it **damage** it?

items.label: Tablet off, adult uses a soft, dry brush
Take it to a repair shop
Poke the fluff out with a pin
Scrape it out with a paper clip
Rinse the port under the tap

cards.explanation: Cables and sockets first, then something **soft and dry** with an adult, or a repair shop. **Metal** can cause a [[short circuit]], and **water** can ruin it.
cards.hint: Remember the two things that must never go in a port.
cards.nudge: Pins and paper clips are metal, and water is just as risky.

cards.title: When a battery swells
cards.body:
Old or damaged **lithium-ion** batteries (in phones and laptops) can **swell**: the case bulges, the screen lifts, or the trackpad (touch pad) is pushed up.

A swollen battery can catch fire if it's pressed or punctured. Stop using the device, don't press it, and get help from an adult or a repair shop.

cards.prompt: An old laptop's case is **bulging** and its trackpad is pushed up. What should you do?

options.text: Stop using it, unplug it, and tell an adult
Press the case flat so the trackpad works
options.nudge: Pressing is the risky part: a swollen battery can catch fire if pressed.

options.text: Keep using it, as long as it still turns on
options.nudge: Turning on doesn't make it safe; a bulge can mean the battery is swelling.

cards.explanation: A bulge often means a swollen [[lithium battery|lithium-ion]], which can catch fire if pressed, bent or punctured. Stop, unplug it, keep it away from anything that can burn, and **tell an adult**. A repair shop can replace it safely.
cards.hint: What did the last card say is dangerous to do to a swollen battery?

cards.prompt: You're gaming on your bed with the phone plugged in.

steps.text: The phone is really hot, and a message says **"Phone needs to cool down."**

choices.text: Put it in the freezer to cool it quickly
choices.consequence: Sudden cold can make water droplets form inside. Let it cool slowly.

choices.text: Ignore it and keep playing until the level ends
choices.consequence: It will slow down to protect itself, and the heat wears out the battery.

choices.text: Stop, unplug it, and rest it on a table
choices.consequence: It cools down safely in a few minutes.

steps.text: A week later, the back looks **puffed up** and the screen is lifting.

choices.text: Stop using it; take it to a repair shop with an adult
choices.consequence: A puffed-up phone often has a swollen battery; a repair shop can replace it safely.

choices.text: Push the screen gently back into place
choices.consequence: Pressing a swollen battery can make it catch fire. Leave it alone and get help.

cards.explanation: Overheating? **Stop, unplug and cool it slowly**, never in the freezer. Puffed up? It may be a **swollen battery**: stop using it, don't press it, and get help from an adult or a repair shop.
cards.hint: Cool it gently, not suddenly; if something looks swollen, hands off.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- **Brightness, location and background apps** drain batteries most. **Heat** wears them out.
- Won't charge? Another cable first. Never metal or water in the port.
- Bulging device? Stop using it, don't press it, get help.
